title: Graph Diffusion Transformers are In-Context Molecular Designers
claim: A single model conditions on small sets of score-example demonstrations to handle many diverse tasks, pretrained broadly and applied to new downstream tasks.
layout: 5 columns, left-to-right, demo boxes above query, arrow header spanning top
description: The figure has five vertical columns. A header runs across the top: 'Task and Descriptions' and 'Pretraining with Millions of Tasks' in red with an arrow, then an ellipsis and a green 'Downstream' arrow. Each column starts with a short text description of a task: cytotoxicity, ADME, binding affinity, polymer thermal conductivity, and finetuning Osimertinib. Below each description is a light-blue box holding four (score, molecule) pairs in large parentheses, with molecular structure drawings. A blue brace and arrow labeled 'Demos' lead down to a query row. The query has a target score of 1.00 and a molecule to generate. In the downstream column the query molecule is a red question mark on a graph icon, which shows the model must design a new molecule. The blue boxes draw the eye first.
caption: In-context molecular design with DemoDiff. Each demo is defined as a score–molecule pair, and a set of them forms the task context as conditions. After pretraining on large and diverse tasks, DemoDiff serves as a foundation model for designing molecules in new task contexts. Scores represent relative distances to the target and are converted from raw labels, as shown in Section 3.3.
abstract: In-context learning allows large models to adapt to new tasks from a few demonstrations, but it has shown limited success in molecular design. Existing databases such as ChEMBL contain molecular properties spanning millions of biological assays, yet labeled data for each property remain scarce. To address this limitation, we introduce demonstration-conditioned diffusion models (DemoDiff), which define task contexts using a small set of molecule-score examples instead of text descriptions. These demonstrations guide a denoising Transformer to generate molecules aligned with target properties. For scalable pretraining, we develop a new molecular tokenizer with Node Pair Encoding that represents molecules at the motif level, requiring 5.5$\times$ fewer nodes. We curate a dataset containing millions of context tasks from multiple sources covering both drugs and materials, and pretrain a 0.7-billion-parameter model on it. Across 33 design tasks in six categories, DemoDiff matches or surpasses language models 100-1000$\times$ larger and achieves an average rank of 3.63 compared to 5.25-10.20 for domain-specific approaches. These results position DemoDiff as a molecular foundation model for in-context molecular design. Our code is available at https://github.com/liugangcode/DemoDiff.
